atAGlance: Bò lá lốt is beef wrapped in betel leaves, usually with grilled aroma, herbs, rice paper, and sweet-sour fish-sauce dip.
whatItIs: Bò lá lốt is seasoned beef wrapped in aromatic lá lốt leaves and grilled. It is often eaten with herbs, rice paper, noodles, and fish-sauce dip so the smoky leaf perfumes the whole bite.
howToEnjoy: Wrap a beef roll with herbs, noodles, and rice paper if served, then dip lightly in the fish-sauce dip. The lá lốt aroma should stay noticeable.
howLocalsOrder: Order bò lá lốt as a shared grilled snack. Ask for extra rice paper or herbs if you want to eat it the local wrap-and-dip way.
worthKnowing: In Vietnam, lá lốt is piper lolot, often called wild betel leaf; it gives the beef a peppery herbal smell travelers remember.
goodToKnow: Rice paper may be served depending on the shop; if you want to wrap, ask for rice paper.
